_note: Example spec for dsh-health-readout. Copy it to your data directory as readings.json
(default: ~/.dsh-health-readout/readings.json) and edit the paths to match your machine.
Keys starting with _ are ignored. Every reading needs: id, source.kind, healthy.op, blind.
Paths are relative to the data directory unless absolute; ~ and ${dataDir} are expanded.
The plugin never writes anything — it only reads what you point it at.

readings.title: The heartbeat file was written recently
readings.blind: Says a writer touched the file; it cannot tell whether the writer is healthy or just alive.

readings.title: The service is listening and answering
readings.blind: One request at one moment. It cannot see a service that is up but wrong.

readings.title: Queue depth is under the ceiling
readings.blind: A single sample. A queue that drains and refills between samples looks identical to a quiet one.

readings.title: Process memory is below the cap
readings.blind: Reads the last recorded sample, not the live process; a fast climb between samples is invisible.

readings.title: No ERROR lines in the recent log window
readings.blind: Counts matches inside a byte window, not the whole file — the window size is reported with the reading.

readings.title: At least one record file exists
readings.blind: Counts files, not contents: an empty-but-present file counts as present.
